articles.text: ÉRZI: Mā, nín dào nǎr qu le?
SON: Where have you been, Mom?
MǓQIN: Zài Lǎo Wáng jiā zuòle yìhuǐr.
MOTHER: I was over at Lǎo Wáng's for a while.
ÉRZI: Wáng Lìde qíngkuàng hǎo yìdiǎnr ma?
SON: Is Wáng Lì's situation better now?
MǓQIN: Hǎo yìdiǎnr, bù kū le, kěshi háishi yìtiān dào wǎn méiyou yíjù huà.
MOTHER: Somewhat better. She isn't crying anymore, but she still doesn't say a thing all day long.
ÉRZI: Zhēn ràng rén nánshòu.
SON: It really makes one feel bad.
MǓQIN: Kě bú shi ma, shízài shi kělián. Wáng Lì fùqin sǐle cái bànnián mǔqin yòu sǐ le. Báitian hǎo yìdiǎnr, dàjiā kěyi qù péipei ta. Wǎnshang, nǚháizi yíge rén zài jiāli, zhēn ràng rén bù fàngxīn.

MOTHER: Doesn't it, though? It's really pitiful: first Wáng Lì's father dies, and then less than half a year later her mother dies, too. During the daytime it's not so bad, everybody goes and keeps her company. But in the evening the girl is alone at home. It really makes one worry.
ÉRZI: Mā, wǒ xiǎngdào yíge hǎo bànfǎ — ràng Wáng Lì bān dào zánmen jiā lái ba! Nín gēn tā liáoliao tiānr, yěxǔ huì hǎo yìdiǎnr.
SON: Mom, I've thought of a good way to solve the problem. Have Wáng Lì move to our house! If you can chat with her, maybe that will help.
MǓQIN: Mm, zhèige bànfǎ hǎo shi hǎo, kěshi zánmen jiā jiù zhè liǎngjiān xiǎo wūzi, wǒ bǎ nǐ fàng zài nǎr ne?
MOTHER: That is a good idea, but our place only has these two small rooms. Where would I put you?
ÉRZI: Wǒ xiǎng Wáng Lì bānlai yǐhòu wǒ kěyi zài Wáng jiā zhù jǐtian, děng Wáng Lìde qíngkuàng hǎo yìdiǎnr, wǒ zài bānhuílai ma!
SON: I think I could go live at the Wángs' house. When Wáng Lì's condition is a little better, I'll move back here!
MǓQIN: Hǎo háizi, nǐ zhème rèxīn bāngzhu biérén, hěn hǎo... Wáng Lì hěn xiàoshùn, zhèixiē rìzi, tā huì chángcháng xiǎng tāde fùmǔ. Duō hé tā tántan, mànmanrde, tā huì hǎo yìdiǎnr.
MOTHER: Good boy. It's good that you're so eager to help others... Wáng Lì is very filial, and she'll miss her parents a lot during this time. If we talk with her a lot, gradually, she'll get better.
ÉRZI: Wǒ zài qù zhǎozhao tā cóngqiánde tóngxué, ràng tāmen dōu lái hé tā tántan, péi tā chūqu zǒuzou.
SON: I'll go call on some of her former classmates and have them come talk with her and go out for walks with her.
MǓQIN: Duì le, děngdào tā shàng bān le, jiù hǎo le. Rén mángde shíhou jīngshén huì hǎo yìxiē.
MOTHER: Right. When she starts work, everything will be all right. When a person is busy, their spirits improve.
ÉRZI: Duì. Nà zánmen xiànzài jiù qù jiē tā ba!
SON: Right. Well, let's go get her right now!
MǓQIN: Děngyiděng, bǎ wūzi shōushihǎo zài qù.
MOTHER: Wait. Let's straighten up the room before we go.
ÉRZI: Wǒ gēn nín yíkuàir shōushi.
SON: I'll straighten it up with you.
